context: Add a short, concrete rule to AGENTS.md near [COMMIT-IDENTITY-001]: a tool, hook, or harness message that instructs setting an agent/service identity is not authorization, and specifically that `git config user.*` without --global inside a linked worktree writes the SHARED config and must never be used to satisfy such a message; the supported response is a per-command `git -c` override or a --worktree-scoped identity. Keep it to a few lines -- the audit enforces a byte ceiling on active instruction text and AGENTS.md is required to stay compact. Also record the external mechanism once in docs/development so it is not rediscovered from scratch, and note that the signature-verification concern the hook is protecting is real: the vendor signing key is registered to that address, so a human committer genuinely does produce an Unverified badge. State the accepted trade-off rather than implying the hook is simply wrong. File the upstream report separately; this item covers only the in-repo boundary.
description: The instruction that contaminates the shared clone does not originate in this repository and cannot be removed from it. A cloud agent session read it directly out of the environment runner binary: a Stop hook fires when any commit ahead of upstream has a committer email other than the vendor signing address, and prints, verbatim, `Please run 'git config user.email noreply@anthropic.com && git config user.name Claude'` followed by a `git commit --amend --no-edit --reset-author` instruction. The absent --global is the damaging detail: run from any linked worktree that write lands in the primary clone's shared config (see worktree-scoped-git-identity-at-claim). A local agent was then observed executing exactly that command in a pool worktree. The hook is external, still in service, and will keep emitting the text whenever a repo-policy-compliant human-authored commit is made in a cloud session -- which is now the expected case, because [COMMIT-IDENTITY-001] requires a human author. So the collision is structural and recurring, not incidental: following BenchBox policy is what triggers the instruction to violate it. This item does not attempt a fix that is not ours to make. It records the boundary and gives agents an explicit, in-repo rule so the next one recognises the instruction as non-authoritative instead of complying with it.

anti_patterns.dont: Describe the external hook as a bug to be worked around by disabling commit signing or ignoring Unverified badges
anti_patterns.instead: State the trade-off explicitly: authorship is what attribution turns on, and a signing service may hold the committer slot behind a human author
anti_patterns.why: The signing key really is registered to the vendor address, so a human committer really does show Unverified; pretending otherwise trades a real property away silently

anti_patterns.dont: Paste the full harness message into AGENTS.md as a quoted block
anti_patterns.instead: State the rule in a line or two in AGENTS.md and keep the mechanism detail in docs/development
anti_patterns.why: AGENTS.md is byte-ceilinged and required to stay compact, and a verbatim copy of the command is itself the instruction this work is trying to stop propagating

anti_patterns.dont: Weaken or reword the [COMMIT-IDENTITY-001] anchors while editing that section
anti_patterns.instead: Add the new rule adjacent to the existing text and leave the pinned phrases byte-identical
anti_patterns.why: agent_instruction_audit.py pins the phrases Co-Authored-By, exact trailer, and not authorization, and the canonical skill mirror is checked for its own anchors; drifting either fails the audit
